title: Bounties are denominated in USD but paid in USDS at par, with adjustment only past a one percent deviation
content:
A.2.11.1.1.3.3.1 states that "[p]ayments are denominated in USD. However, payouts are done in USDS assuming a full 1:1 ratio with the USD. However, if the price of USDS deviates from the USD value by more than 1%, the amount of USDS will be adjusted."

Three things are happening at once. The obligation is a dollar obligation, so the researcher is promised value not tokens. Settlement is in Sky's own liability, so Sky pays in an instrument it issues rather than in acquired dollars. And a 1% tolerance band means the par assumption is not corrected for small deviations.

Inside that band, the payee bears the loss. A researcher paid at par while USDS trades at 0.995 receives 0.5% less than promised, and there is no symmetry argument that helps them — the adjustment is described as a response to deviation, not as a two-sided mark.

The band is a reasonable operational simplification: recomputing every payment against an oracle price adds process for immaterial amounts. It is also a small but real transfer of Sky's own peg risk to the people it is paying for finding peg-threatening bugs. On the largest bounties, tranched over months under A.2.11.1.1.3.3.2, the payee is exposed to that band repeatedly.
description: Inside the 1% band the whitehat absorbs any USDS depeg; beyond it the USDS amount is adjusted, making the peg tolerance an explicit allocation of currency risk to the payee.
